items.utility_name: Consolidated Edison Co of New York (Con Edison)
items.program_name: Value Stack (Value of Distributed Energy Resources / VDER) Tariff
items.incentive_structure: component-based export credit ($/kWh + $/kW) applied as monetary bill credits
items.incentive_value_usd: $0.65/kW-mo residential and $1.03/kW-mo small commercial CBC (2026, Value Stack PV)
items.event_limits: Phase Two eligibility: on-site DG >750 kW plus remote net metered and community DG of any size; CHP excluded. Phase One (pre-7/26/2018 qualifiers) uses $/kW-yr DRV/LSRV and a Market Transition Credit
items.on_peak_window: DRV: assigned 4-hour window on summer non-holiday weekdays Jun 24-Sep 15; ICAP Alt 2: 2pm-7pm Jun 24-Aug 31
items.export_compensation: Value Stack credit = LBMP (day-ahead energy) + ICAP capacity (Alt 1 all-hours $/kWh, Alt 2 concentrated 240-245 summer afternoon hrs 2-7pm Jun 24-Aug 31, or Alt 3 $/kW-month coincident-peak - Alt 3 required for dispatchable/paired storage) + Environmental (REC or social cost of carbon $/kWh) + DRV ($/kWh on export in an assigned 4-hr summer weekday window Jun 24-Sep 15) + LSRV ($/kW-event in designated high-value areas until MW cap) + Community Credit for CDG. Values vary hourly and by utility/zone - see utility Value Stack calculator
items.stackable_with: NY-Sun; NYSERDA Retail Energy Storage Incentive; utility DR programs

Commercial standby is Rate Code 682 with eleven sub-rate codes; optional residential standby rates are also offered. Mandatory for about 72 existing commercial customers, optional for most others (SC-5, SC-7, SC-10, SC-13, unmetered and non-AMI customers may not opt in). items.utility_name: New York Independent System Operator
items.program_name: Dual Participation - NYISO Aggregation plus utility DR program (CSRP / DLRP / DLM)
items.incentive_structure: No separate payment - this is the rule permitting a DER to earn both NYISO market revenue and utility DR program revenue
items.event_limits: PERMITTED. An Aggregation containing DER that also participate in programs meeting distribution-system needs in the NYCA must notify NYISO of dual participation at enrollment (Market Participant User's Guide Section 1.2); the Aggregation's NYISO offers must be constructed so the Aggregation is scheduled by NYISO whenever it operates to meet the non-wholesale commitment (Services Tariff 4.1.11). NYISO confirms CSRP, DLRP and DLM are covered by this categorization. Dual-participation requirements are scheduled to change when NYISO implements its Order 2222-compliant tariff (targeted end of 2026)
items.tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Section 4.1.11; Market Participant User's Guide Section 1.2
items.stackable_with: Con Edison CSRP; Con Edison DLRP; Joint Utilities Dynamic Load Management (DLM); NOT stackable with NYISO SCR or EDRP

items.utility_name: Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corp
items.program_name: Value Stack (Value of Distributed Energy Resources / VDER) Tariff
items.incentive_structure: component-based export credit ($/kWh + $/kW) applied as monetary bill credits
items.incentive_value_usd: $0.84/kW-mo residential and $1.28/kW-mo small commercial CBC (2026, Value Stack PV)
items.event_limits: Phase Two eligibility: on-site DG >750 kW plus remote net metered and community DG of any size; CHP excluded. Phase One (pre-7/26/2018 qualifiers) uses $/kW-yr DRV/LSRV and a Market Transition Credit
items.on_peak_window: DRV: assigned 4-hour window on summer non-holiday weekdays Jun 24-Sep 15; ICAP Alt 2: 2pm-7pm Jun 24-Aug 31
items.export_compensation: Value Stack credit = LBMP (day-ahead energy) + ICAP capacity (Alt 1 all-hours $/kWh, Alt 2 concentrated 240-245 summer afternoon hrs 2-7pm Jun 24-Aug 31, or Alt 3 $/kW-month coincident-peak - Alt 3 required for dispatchable/paired storage) + Environmental (REC or social cost of carbon $/kWh) + DRV ($/kWh on export in an assigned 4-hr summer weekday window Jun 24-Sep 15) + LSRV ($/kW-event in designated high-value areas until MW cap) + Community Credit for CDG. Values vary hourly and by utility/zone - see utility Value Stack calculator
items.stackable_with: NY-Sun; NYSERDA Retail Energy Storage Incentive; utility DR programs

items.utility_name: New York Independent System Operator
items.program_name: DER Aggregation - eligibility sizing rules (10 kW DER / 100 kW Aggregation / 20 MW injection cap)
items.incentive_structure: Eligibility gate - no payment
items.event_limits: Minimum capability of each individual DER (including a Demand Side Resource) participating in an Aggregation is 10 kW; where a DER includes multiple assets of different technologies at the facility, EACH asset must independently meet 10 kW. Minimum size of a DER Aggregation is 100 kW; an Aggregation that offers a combination of Energy injections, Energy withdrawals and/or Demand Reduction must be able to offer at least 100 kW of each. Maximum Injection Limit for an injecting facility in an Aggregation is 20 MW; there is no size cap on Demand Reduction resources. All DER in an Aggregation must be on the SAME Transmission Node and therefore in the same NYISO Load Zone. A DER facility has a single point of interconnection and a single utility account number, and may participate in only one Aggregation at a time. FERC found the 10 kW minimum just and reasonable on April 15 2024 and confirmed it is not a temporary measure
items.tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Sections 4.1.10 and 4.1.10.1; NYISO Manual 38 (Aggregation Manual)
items.stackable_with: Resources under 10 kW remain eligible for EDRP, the SCR program (including Small Customer Aggregation) and NY State and utility DER programs

items.export_compensation: Electing standby service moves the customer from Phase One net metering to the VDER Value Stack
